Subject: Q3 right-size & contract evolution proposal

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the sync yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together a short health recap and three pragmatic options so OpenRetail can keep latency stable while controlling unit economics as you scale into Q3. Key highlights (Q1–Q2):

- Total token spend: ~38M tokens (70% generation, 30% embeddings)
- Projected Q3 midpoint: ~55M tokens based on current adoption curves and the new personalization pipeline
- Observed P95 text generation latency: 210ms stable on dedicated variants; occasional P99 spikes to ~680ms during nightly batch runs
- Cost drivers: heavy repeated generation with limited prefix caching, two models in prod with different quant profiles

Attachments: OpenRetail_Q1-Q2_token_report.xlsx, latency_summary_Q2.pdf (see breakdown by model and per-route token mix).

Recommendation — three paths depending on appetite for predictability vs flexibility:

1) Right-size committed tier (recommended): 12-month commit at 45M tokens/mo equivalent (staged ramp over 3 months), 6% unit price reduction vs current overage rate, includes 1M burst credits per quarter.
2) Short-term flexibility: 6-month term with higher burst allowance, no deep discount, automatic fit-back to hosted variants during surges.
3) Conservative: Keep month-to-month; enable prefix caching and quantization audit (Redwood Optimize) to bring down unit usage ~12% within 8 weeks.

Ask: could you confirm which path you prefer and whether Procurement needs an SOW/addendum to start drafting? If you want, I can share a draft MOA and a mutual action plan this week.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Karthik —

Appreciate the detailed recap. Quick follow-ups before we push to Procurement:

- Can you provide the token split by model name (gen vs embed) and the % of traffic tied to the personalization pipeline specifically? We need that for our cost allocation.
- Procurement will want to see SLA language around latency (our internal goal is P95 < 250ms for inference endpoints). Would Redwood consider a small SLA credit if monthly P95 breaches 250ms more than twice?
- On discounts: our CFO asked whether you have flexibility on the proposed 6% — would you consider a one-time onboarding credit or a front-loaded discount for the first 3 months to help offset migration costs?

I'll attach our internal procurement checklist (see procurement thread). If you can send a draft MOA (with proposed metric thresholds), we'll have Procurement review and loop in legal.

Thanks —
Alex
Head of ML Platform | OpenRetail

Folks — forwarding Alex's reply and the asks from Procurement. Quick read: they want

- model-level token split by name (we have that in the token report)
- SLA credit proposal for P95 > 250ms (they want it tied to monthly breaches)
- either a short front-loaded discount or onboarding credit for first 3 months

My recommended concession: agree to an 8% front-loaded discount applied to first 3 billing cycles and include a targeted SLA credit (0.5% credit for each month with >2 P95 breaches, capped at 1.5% quarterly). Keep the right-size commit at 12 months but allow a 90-day ramp window. Ask Sales Ops to prepare a draft MOA with those terms so we can send to them.

Why: keeps economics reasonable, addresses the CFO ask, and gives us predictable committed revenue. If Legal pushes back on SLA caps we can make it a credit-only remedy (no refunds).

Attachments: draft-moa-rightsize-v2.pdf (I pulled the base terms into a one-pager).

Thoughts? If you approve I'll send the update to Alex and include a DocuSign link for signature.

— Karthik

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the patience while we ran this through Sales Ops and Legal. Based on your asks, Redwood is prepared to move forward with the following final items:

1) Commercials: 12-month committed path (right-size) with a 90-day ramp. Commitment target: equivalent of 45M tokens/month at tiered pricing. We will apply an 8% front-loaded discount to the first three billing cycles (applied as credit).

2) SLA & credits: We will include an objective SLA for inference latency: P95 < 250ms target. If monthly P95 exceeds 250ms more than twice that month, we will issue a 0.5% credit on that month’s invoice. Credits are capped at 1.5% per quarter. (Legal approved credit-only remedy.)

3) Onboarding support: 1M burst credits per quarter for Q3 and Q4; Redwood Optimize will run a quantization/prefix cache audit to target ~10–12% token reduction within 8 weeks post-signature.

4) Next steps: I've attached the updated MOA (draft-moa-rightsize-v2.pdf) and a one-page mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_openretail.xlsx).
